---
title: "The Essence of Data Visualisation"
subtitle: "PyCon Africa 2026"
---

Every plot and every table you have ever seen is doing the same thing:
mapping data values to visual properties. A scatter plot maps two columns to
x and y positions. A colour-coded table maps values to a colour scale. A bar
chart and a pie chart are the same mapping in different coordinate systems.

Once you see this, you stop memorising chart types and start *reasoning*
about visualisation. You can look at any graphic — a plot, a table, a
dashboard — and ask one question: **"what maps to what?"**

In this two-hour, hands-on workshop you will:

- learn the single idea behind all data visualisation,
- put it into practice with **plotnine** for plots and **great-tables** for
  tables,
- and use it to dissect a real case where a table went wrong: the Uganda
  2024 Census tribal population figures, where a row transposition error
  triggered a national conversation.

Everything runs in your browser — no installation needed. Every code block
is editable and runnable.

By the end you will be able to:

1. explain what it means to map data to visual properties, and use that to
   reason about any visualisation,
2. build layered plots with plotnine,
3. build structured tables with great-tables,
4. decide when a table serves readers better than a plot, and vice versa,
5. spot data errors through deliberate visualisation choices.

## Before you arrive

Nothing to install. If you'd like to follow along on your own machine
instead of the browser, install the packages:

```bash
pip install plotnine great-tables pandas
```
